RFC7950-6.1.3-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-09 after 180df07922 (Resolve returns *yang.Resolved, one Resolve per Loader; process, checkExtensions, checkPatterns, checkStructure still all run and join, refusals unchanged): tagged units changed only in the 64-char tail of ModuleLoadAccepted (schema.GetEntry from the Resolved); cases unchanged, package green. RFC 6.1.3: 'The backslash MUST NOT be followed by any other character.' Prior judgement, still true: Re-judged 2026-10-09; the case edited in ModuleLoadRefused is another row's. Negative: case "bad escape" (description "bad \q escape", the only fault) requires an error containing "escape". Positive: case "valid escapes" loads \t \n \" \\ in a double-quoted string. Probe 2026-10-09: a single-quoted 'bad \q kept', where backslash is not special, loads, so the refusal is scoped to double quotes as Section 6.1.3 scopes it.

RFC7950-6.2-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-09 after 180df07922 (Resolve returns *yang.Resolved, one Resolve per Loader; process, checkExtensions, checkPatterns, checkStructure still all run and join, refusals unchanged): the 64-character leaf is now read from schema.GetEntry of the returned Resolved, same assertions. RFC 6.2: 'Implementations MUST support identifiers up to 64 characters in length and MAY support longer identifiers.' Prior judgement, still true: {single-polarity} on the row. (a) forbidden: refusing or truncating a 64-character identifier. (b) TestRFC7950ModuleLoadAccepted loads a module whose leaf name is 64 characters (require.NoError on AddModuleFromText and Resolve) and assert.NotNil(entry.Dir[long]), which goes red if the name were refused or shortened.

RFC7950-6.5-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-09 after 180df07922 (Resolve returns *yang.Resolved, one Resolve per Loader; process, checkExtensions, checkPatterns, checkStructure still all run and join, refusals unchanged): cases unchanged. RFC 6.5: 'References to identifiers defined in external modules MUST be qualified with appropriate prefixes'. Prior judgement, still true: Re-judged 2026-10-09; unchanged cases. Clause 1: ModuleLoadRefused case "external typedef without prefix" (type port with ext imported) requires "unknown type", against Accepted case "prefixed external and bare local" (ext:port and bare local l load). Clause 2 (MAY): Accepted case "extension with own and import prefix" loads m:e under the module's own prefix. The submodule half of the MAY clause is not driven; a MAY imposes no refusal.

RFC7950-7.19-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-09 after 180df07922 (Resolve returns *yang.Resolved, one Resolve per Loader; process, checkExtensions, checkPatterns, checkStructure still all run and join, refusals unchanged): only the ModuleLoadAccepted tail changed. RFC 7.19: 'the substatements MUST be YANG statements, including extensions defined using "extension" statements.' The earlier finding that sources was keyed by file name no longer holds at HEAD: sourcedModules.texts is keyed by *yang.Module (Parse binds each module added by a parse to its text). Revert records on AddModuleFromText for the ModuleLoadAccepted/Refused tags are owed a re-record. Prior judgement, still true: Re-judged 2026-10-09 after 6c06cb43af/037cc25e29. Sentence 1: TestRFC7950ExtensionUsageSubstatementsAreYANGStatements refuses m:e "x" { bogus "y"; } against description and nested m:e twins. Sentence 2 (Section 14 rules) now whole: substatements are resolved against the embedded RFC ABNF (resolveProduction) and checked for argument grammar (config maybe, namespace not a URI, path a / ../a[), cardinality (two type, two description; one type + two must loads), required substatements and blocks (leaf without type, list without data-def, refine with no block) and context forms (deviate add/not-supported mixing, type-body alternatives, augment absolute vs descendant), each tagged test with a revert record on its producer. Independent probe 2026-10-09 of ~70 valid unusual forms under a usage (quoted/unquoted/single-quoted args, + concatenation, nested usages at depth, leafref require-instance, multiple leaf-list defaults, deviate add/replace/delete in full, if-feature expressions with extra whitespace, path predicates with WSP, IPv6/percent URIs, refine across comments/newlines/tabs/UTF-8/CRLF, nested module/submodule) all load; config TRUE, max-elements 0/007, fraction-digits 19, deref() path, refine x; via comment or concatenation, empty input/augment are refused. The ModuleLoadRefused/Accepted tags drive the extension DEFINITION (extension e { bogus }), governed by the Section 14 extension-stmt rule, a neighbouring rule; their claims state what the body checks but do not bear on this sentence.

RFC7950-7.2.2-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after bb173975ea). Read at rfc/full/rfc7950.txt Section 7.2.2: "A submodule MUST only be included by either the module to which it belongs or another submodule that belongs to that module." Producer: checkStructure (joined by Resolve) runs moduleIncludeErrors over every loaded module and submodule (sourceModules); it resolves the including unit's owner (its own name, or its belongs-to) and refuses an include whose submodule belongs to another module with ErrIncludeBelongsTo. TestRFC7950SubmoduleIncludedOnlyByItsModule covers both clauses in both polarities: negatives refuse module a including s (belongs-to b) and submodule a-s of a including s, each requiring the text "belongs to module b"; positives load module a including a-t and a-s including sibling a-t. Module b is loaded and includes s in the negatives, so only the belongs-to differs. Independent overlay mutants (tags ze_core ze_bgp), each red on an assertion: owner ignores belongs-to (submodule-sibling positive red), modules skipped (submodule negative red), submodules skipped (module negative red), comparison always passes (both negatives red), comparison always fails (both positives red). Two equivalent-in-test mutants survive: dropping either lookup in includedSubmodule (include.Module, or the SubModules map fallback) leaves the test green because the other still finds the submodule; the redundancy changes no verdict but no test proves the fallback is needed. The recorded revert tuples (panic in moduleIncludeErrors) prove reach only. {gap} removed from the row in bb173975ea; Ze ships no submodule of its own, so the check guards loaded module sets.

RFC7950-7.21.5-2.note: Re-judged 2026-10-20 (independent judge, after 4bf9935e38). Section 7.21.5: "There MUST NOT be any circular dependencies among \"when\" expressions." walkTree's change is the case-data descent through schemaChild and the mandatory checks in requireMandatoryChildren; no when expression is parsed, ordered or evaluated anywhere in config/yang, so neither the evaluation order nor the cycle rule is applied. Ze's modules declare no when today. {gap} stands. Owned by spec-config-yang-when-unique-choice.

RFC7950-7.3.2-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-09 after 180df07922 (Resolve returns *yang.Resolved, one Resolve per Loader; process, checkExtensions, checkPatterns, checkStructure still all run and join, refusals unchanged): the positive now reads the leaf from schema.GetEntry of the returned Resolved, same assertion (Yuint8). RFC 7.3.2: 'The "type" statement, which MUST be present, defines the base type from which this type is derived.' negative: a typedef with only a description refused; positive: the same typedef with type uint8 loads and the leaf using it resolves to Yuint8 (proves the type defines the base type). Twins differ by the type statement alone, so the loose "type" substring cannot be met by another fault. Records on Resolve. Those Resolve revert records no longer verify (unit-changed) and are owed a re-record.

RFC7950-7.3.4-1.note: all three sentences, both polarities, isolated by one-statement twins: (1) typedef default in/out of its own range (old pair, records on validateLeafDefaults); (2) a leaf of the typedef with no default carries 5, a narrowing leaf or typedef giving a new default carries 7/8 with no error (record on yangToLeaf); (3) a leaf and a typedef narrowing 1..10 to 6..10 with no new default each refused naming "5" (record on validateTypedefDefault).

RFC7950-7.6.1-1.note: Both halves of the no-ancestor branch are now tagged: TestRFC7950LeafDefaultUsedWhenAbsent (top-level leaf gets its default) and TestApplyDefaults_NonPresenceContainer (a leaf whose only ancestor is a non-presence container absent from the data: ApplyDefaults creates the container and fills 90/120, both values asserted). Negative TestRFC7950LeafDefaultNotUsedWhenSet (a set value keeps its value) is valid. Observed-red records: applyChildDefault for both RFC units, applyContainerDefault for the non-presence unit.

RFC7950-7.6.1-2.note: Re-judged 2026-10-20 (independent judge, after 7f34543a08). Section 7.6.1: "Otherwise, if this ancestor is a case node, the default value MUST be used if any node from the case exists in the data tree or the case node is the choice's default case, and if no nodes from any other case exist in the data tree." Producer: ApplyDefaults now asks choiceMembers.skipsDefaults before each child; yangToContainer and yangToList record the goyang entry of every child a choice holds (cases.record in both the container and the list choice branch), mergeContainer and mergeNode carry it (adopt), and skipsDefaults calls yang.CaseInEffect for leaves and non-presence containers, leaving presence containers and lists to their own existing-ancestor rule. CaseInEffect climbs every choice between the node and its data parent: in effect when exactly one case holds data and it is this one, or none does and this is the default case; two cases holding data put no case in effect. Positive TestRFC7950CaseDefaultsFollowTheCaseInEffect asserts exact defaults for the case holding data (a2, c2, inside a list entry) and the default case (b1 and the non-presence container bc/bd) with no data; negative TestRFC7950CaseDefaultsIgnoredOutsideTheCaseInEffect asserts exact maps: no other case's default, no non-default case without data, nothing when two cases hold data, nothing for a choice with no default case, list entry, merged container. Mutant records on skipsDefaults (data->nil; inverted predicate) verify. Judge probes via -overlay, all RFC-correct: nested choice in the default case (no data -> outer default case leaf and inner default case x; inner non-default case data -> its default plus the outer case's default; data in another outer case -> only that case's defaults; data in both outer cases -> none); default leaf in a non-presence container of a non-default case (not created with no data, created when a sibling of that case holds data, filled when the container itself is present); shorthand cases; nested choice inside a case container. Scope: no shipped ApplyDefaults caller defaults a node that holds a choice today (bgp peer, rib distance, filter-modify, the tunnel case container), so the proof is at ApplyDefaults over yangToNode, the converter the config schema uses; the reference walk reads the same CaseInEffect. go test ./internal/component/config/ ./internal/component/config/yang/ green at HEAD.

RFC7950-7.6.1-3.note: §7.6.1 third branch, both polarities on one isolated unit (own schema build and map per subtest). Positive: an existing presence container and an existing list entry each receive their child leaf's default through ApplyDefaults. Negative: with both ancestors absent ApplyDefaults creates neither and the map stays empty. Records: positive on applyContainerDefault (revert); negative on the targeted mutant 'c.Presence' -> 'false' (a presence container treated as non-presence), observed red on the ancestor-absent subtest, so the negative discriminates the rule rather than a panic.

RFC7950-7.6.1-4.note: Re-judged 2026-10-20 (independent judge, after 7f34543a08). Section 7.6.1: "Note that if the leaf or any of its ancestors has a \"when\" condition or \"if-feature\" expression that evaluates to \"false\", then the default value is not in use." ApplyDefaults changed only to skip children whose case is not in effect (choiceMembers.skipsDefaults -> yang.CaseInEffect); it still evaluates no when and no if-feature, so a default under a false when stays in use. The {gap} annotation remains accurate. Owned by plan/pre-release/spec-config-yang-when-unique-choice.md.

RFC7950-7.6.5-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-20 (independent auditor, after 4bf9935e38). Section 7.6.5: "If "mandatory" is "true", the behavior of the constraint depends on the type of the leaf's closest ancestor node in the schema tree that is not a non-presence container (see Section 7.5.1): o If no such ancestor exists in the schema tree, the leaf MUST exist." Tested "the leaf MUST exist"; Gap "If no such ancestor exists in the schema tree"; Producer internal/component/config/validate_sections.go::ValidateCustomSections; annotation unchanged. The only change under this row is walkTree's fingerprint: its per-level mandatory scan moved verbatim into requireMandatoryChildren, which for every non-choice child keeps the same three checks (mandatory leaf absent from data, an absent non-presence child descended by requireMandatoryUnderAbsent, an absent leaf-list with min-elements above zero); the mandatory-choice check is unchanged; the case check and the schemaChild key lookup add coverage below a choice and change nothing for a leaf with no qualifying ancestor. Tagged units unchanged and green (go test ./internal/component/config/ ./internal/component/config/yang/); ./le rfc discriminate id RFC7950-7.6.5-1 lists seven records re-recorded over the new walkTree, none stale. The revert-route records answer reachability only, but the scoped negatives assert exact missing paths and the positives zero missing errors once supplied, so the Tested scope stays proven. Gap stands as before: an absent top-level section is not walked (owner ruling 6, 2026-10-12) and bgp router-id and local ASN counted present through EverySessionCarries (rulings of 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-16); a deviation is never conformant, zero whole-requirement credit.

RFC7950-7.6.5-2.note: Re-judged 2026-10-20 (independent auditor, after 4bf9935e38 and 29419d46cf). Read at rfc/full/rfc7950.txt Section 7.6.5: "Otherwise, if this ancestor is a case node, the leaf MUST exist if any node from the case exists in the data tree." The row's {gap} is gone and the code now does it. walkTree resolves each data key through schemaChild, which descends through choice and case entries, so case data is type-checked and walked; requireMandatoryChildren handles a choice child by requireMandatoryInPresentCases, which runs requireMandatoryChildren over every case for which holdsData finds a node in the map holding the choice, and skips the rest. Shapes checked by probe (go test -overlay, nothing written to the tree): a mandatory leaf directly in a case; below non-presence containers a present case holds (walked through schemaChild, then requireMandatoryUnderAbsent); a non-presence container ABSENT inside a case that has another node present is still required (closest qualifying ancestor is the case); a presence container inside a case owes its leaf only when present; a case inside a nested choice (inner choice handled by the IsChoice branch of requireMandatoryChildren on the outer case); an implicit case: goyang's FixChoice wraps each shorthand node in a CaseEntry, so a shorthand container's mandatory leaf is checked against the container's own map and reported as wrap/shc/m, with no false error when supplied. goyang refuses a choice as shorthand of a choice, so that shape cannot be loaded. Negative TestRFC7950MandatoryRequiredWhenCaseExists asserts the exact missing path, the set command and that it is the only missing path for each of the three placements; positive TestRFC7950MandatoryNotRequiredForAbsentCase asserts zero errors with no case present and with each case complete. The .ci drives ze config validate over a gre tunnel with local ip and no remote ip and requires exit 1, the path interface/tunnel[gre0]/encapsulation/gre/remote/ip and the set command. Question 2 judged by my own mutants, not by the records: (A) requireMandatoryInPresentCases checks every case regardless of holdsData: positive goes red in all four subtests and the negative too; (B) it checks no case: negative goes red (leaf in case, leaf in nested case); (C) walkTree reverted to the pre-fix entry.Dir lookup: negative goes red (leaf below containers, empty container), and ze config validate over the .ci's config prints 'configuration valid' and exits 0, so the .ci discriminates the defect it names. The recorded revert breaks (panic in requireMandatoryInPresentCases; panic in schemaChild, which crashes ze at schema load) prove only that the units reach those producers; they are coarse, but they do not weaken this verdict because the mutants above show both polarities fail on the actual non-compliance in each direction. The .ci record is worth re-recording on the mutant route (for example the entry.Dir lookup in walkTree), since a crash at schema load turns every .ci red. Population: the case-scoped mandatory leaves in shipped modules are iface tunnel remote/ip (tunnel-v4/v6-endpoints) and vxlan vni; static and bfd hold mandatory choices (Section 7.9.4, not this row). One reading to note: an empty non-presence container written in a case (gre { }) counts as the case existing, which is the strict reading and fails closed. All tagged units green at HEAD; ./le rfc discriminate id RFC7950-7.6.5-2 lists three records, none stale or unproven.

RFC7950-7.6.5-3.note: Re-judged 2026-10-20 (independent auditor, after 4bf9935e38). Section 7.6.5: "Otherwise, the leaf MUST exist if the ancestor node exists in the data tree." Tagged units unchanged; walkTree's fingerprint changed because the per-level scan moved into requireMandatoryChildren with the same checks for non-choice children (see RFC7950-7.6.5-1), and walkTree now finds data keys through schemaChild. TestRFC7950MandatoryOutsideValidatedSections (bfd auth presence container, both exact paths, from mandatoryFailures) and TestRFC7950MandatoryRequiredWhenAncestorExists (list entry and presence container) are green at HEAD, and ./le rfc discriminate id RFC7950-7.6.5-3 lists four records, none stale. The latent exclusion the previous verdict recorded, that walkTree did not descend into case data so a list or presence container inside a case was never checked, is closed: probe shows a presence container present inside a case with its mandatory leaf absent reported at its path, and the same container absent owing nothing. The revert-route records prove reachability only; the verdict rests on the exact-path negatives and the supplied-leaf positives, which an over-eager or skipped check would turn red. Verdict stands.

RFC7950-7.7.4-1.note: (a) forbidden: a leaf-list default invalid for its type loading; a leaf-list default beside min-elements >= 1 loading. (b) TestRFC7950DefaultInvalidForType: leaf-list range 1..10 default 30 requires an error containing `default "30" is not valid for type uint8`, and leaf-list min-elements 1 default 1 requires "min-elements 1 is invalid"; positive TestRFC7950DefaultValidForType: leaf-list default 3 inside 1..10 with no min-elements, assert.NoError. min-elements above 1 is not cased separately; 1 is the boundary.

RFC7950-7.7.5-1.note: (a) forbidden: accepting a leaf-list or list with fewer entries than min-elements. (b) TestRFC7950MinElementsViolated: leaf-list with 1 of min 2, absent leaf-list with min 1, and list with 1 of min 2 each require.Len 1 and Contains "too few entries: N (minimum M)"; TestRFC7950MinElementsMet: leaf-list at exactly min 2 and list of 2 above min 1 assert.Empty.

RFC7950-7.9.2-2.note: negative: two cases named x in one choice refused as duplicate; positive: cases x and y load, and case x in two different choices loads, which pins the scope to one choice. Records on Resolve. (2026-10-09: tagged units byte-identical, re-stamped for a file shift; the Resolve revert records no longer verify since 180df07922 changed Resolve, re-record owed.)

RFC7950-7.9.4-1.note: Judged 2026-10-12 (independent auditor). Section 7.9.4: "If \"mandatory\" is \"true\", at least one node from exactly one of the choice's case branches MUST exist." Tested "at least one node from"; Gap "exactly one of the choice's case branches"; Producer internal/component/config/yang/validator_mandatory.go::mandatoryPresent. Tested holds: TestMandatoryChoiceSatisfiedByACaseNode reports wrap/kind missing for a container with no node of any case (exact path), and accepts a node of one case and a node of a nested choice's case, so a lookup by the choice name alone, or one that ignores nested choices, goes red; records on mandatoryPresent (positive) and missingMandatory (negative). Real entry: walkTree's mandatory loop reaches it from ValidateCustomSections, so the static route choice action and the iface tunnel encapsulation choice kind are refused when empty. Gap holds: data with nodes from two cases is accepted at the first case node found and no other check compares the cases, so the exactly-one half is unmet; the conditional enforcement under a case or list ancestor in the following paragraph is a separate sentence. Whole requirement earns no credit; spec-config-yang-when-unique-choice.

RFC7950-8.1-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-20 (independent judge, after 4bf9935e38). Section 8.1: "If the constraint is defined on configuration data, it MUST be true in a valid configuration data tree." walkTree now resolves data keys through schemaChild (case data is type-checked and walked) and moves the mandatory scan into requireMandatoryChildren, which also checks cases holding data. It still evaluates no unique (ListNode.Unique is read only by the web UI for display), no choice exclusivity and no when. Judge probe via -overlay: ValidateTree over a choice with data in two cases (alpha and gamma, mandatory leaves supplied) returns zero errors, so a configuration violating Section 8.1's choice constraint is accepted. {gap} stands. Owned by spec-config-yang-when-unique-choice.

RFC7950-8.1-2.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after 9d4a5e79e2). Section 8.1: "The running configuration datastore MUST always be valid." The earlier finding (only config.LoadConfig was driven; no install route) is answered for the reload route: TestRFC7950ReloadInstallsAValidConfig and TestRFC7950ReloadRefusesAConstraintViolation write the file and drive diskConfigLoaders and doReload, the path every SIGHUP and editor reload notifier reaches, and assert the refused reload returns ErrCustomValidation naming the value while the reactor keeps system/host reload-valid-host. TestRFC7950WebCommitRefusesAConstraintViolation shows the web editor commit writes nothing for the same violation. Startup stays covered by the LoadConfig units. Residual: the SSH session editor (session_editor.go) sets no pre-commit validator, so its commit relies on the reload refusal the reload units prove; no tagged unit drives that editor, and none drives the gNMI/API configValidationHook route.

RFC7950-8.1-3.note: Re-judged 2026-10-12, second pass (independent auditor) after 60a74fc04b, 600996fb77, 975428e1b3, 3f1bec74f0 and 84382339ce. SHIFTED only: the tagged units are byte-identical (gate-verified). range: receive-hold-time 2 and port 0 refused ErrTypeRange, 1 and 2 refused and 0, 3, 180, 65535 accepted; pattern: router-id not-an-ip refused ErrTypePattern at errs[0] with session/asn/local supplied so no missing-mandatory error comes first, 192.0.2.1 accepted; length: a 256-char isis hostname refused ErrTypeLength and a within-length one raises no length error. RFC7950-8.1-4.note: Re-judged 2026-10-20 (independent judge, after 4bf9935e38). RFC7950-9.1-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-19 (independent auditor, after 40a03eb762 and db457cb3c2). Section 9.1: "Implementations MUST support all lexical representations specified in this document." Tagged units are unchanged; the cited producers changed. db457cb3c2 splits compound guards in readInstancePredicates and readEqualsQuoted into one guard per operand with identical bodies, no behavior change. 40a03eb762 makes instanceExists a referenceWalk method that compares a leaf-list predicate value with sameValue (canonicalValue of both sides under the leaf-list's type) and selects a list entry through the canonical keyIndex (canonicalKey) instead of the raw map-key address, so a configured value and a default in use now answer the same lexical forms. This resolves the prior judgement's observation that [.='+17'] matched a default 17 but not a configured 17 (Section 9.1: "In particular, any XPath expression evaluations are done using the canonical form if the data type has a canonical form."). The '.' leaf-list-predicate parse, *WSP handling and absent-value refusal that TestRFC7950InstanceIdentifierLeafListPredicate and ...Absent assert are unaffected (string leaf-list: canonicalValue is identity), and the integer, decimal64, binary, bits, leafref and union-default units of the prior judgement stand. All tagged units and TestReferenceCanonicalValueRefusesOther pass at HEAD (go test -tags 'ze_core ze_bgp' over config/yang and config). The canonical comparison is proven by TestRFC7950InstanceIdentifierCanonicalValue under RFC7950-9.13-1, not by a 9.1-1 tag.

RFC7950-9.1-2.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after 2e4be94ae3). Read at rfc/full/rfc7950.txt Section 9.1: "If the data type does not have a canonical form, the format of the value MUST match the data type's lexical representation, but the exact format is implementation dependent." The types are identityref (Section 9.10.4) and instance-identifier (Section 9.13.3). Both prior findings are fixed. (1) Section 9.13.2 "All node names in an instance-identifier value MUST be qualified with explicit namespace prefixes": checkInstanceKeyPrefix now refuses an unprefixed or foreign key prefix; TestRFC7950InstanceIdentifierKeyPrefix (negative) asserts both messages and the accepted rf:name form, and overlay mutants dropping the empty-prefix branch and the entryPrefixed branch each turned it red. (2) Cascade confounding: TestRFC7950IdentityrefFormat now asserts the format check's own message, and TestRFC7950InstanceIdentifierLexical asserts 'not an instance-identifier' for rf:sys and the unprefixed-node message for /sys/mgmt; overlay mutants removing the identifierRefLength check and the leading-slash check turned each red. A probe of further malformed values (rf:1aes, rf:, :aes, trailing space, //rf:sys, an unquoted key value, [0], mismatched and embedded quotes, a space between steps) found each refused with ErrTypeType.

RFC7950-9.3.1-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after 2e4be94ae3). Read at rfc/full/rfc7950.txt Section 9.3.1: "A decimal64 value is lexically represented as an optional sign ("+" or "-"), followed by a sequence of decimal digits, optionally followed by a period ('.') as a decimal indicator and a sequence of decimal digits." The units changed only from validateYangType to ValidateType, which is the same producer path (validateLeafValue with no leaf). validateDecimal64 tests ^[+-]?\d+(\.\d+)?$ (ASCII digits in Go RE2) before the fraction-digits parse. Positive accepts +1.5, -1.5, -10.5, 1, 0.25, 0.0, 10.50; negative refuses .5, 1., +, -, 1.2.3, abc and the empty string with ErrTypeType and 'expected decimal64', with fraction-digits and range refusals asserted as distinct kinds. Each clause of the sentence has a value that would flip if the regexp lost it; records on validateDecimal64 replay.
